answer.line: Both dH and dS are negative: the enthalpy helps, the entropy fights harder as T rises. dG crosses zero at 800 K.

steps: Read the signs first. dH < 0 helps the reaction; dS < 0 fights it, and the -T dS penalty grows with temperature.
So it is spontaneous when cold, not when hot. Find the switch: set dG = 0, so T = dH / dS.
Match the units, then divide: -120,000 J over -150 J/K is 800 K. Below 800 K, dG is negative.

choices.note: dG = 0 at 800 K, and below it the negative dH wins.
The direction is right, but the crossover is off by a factor of ten. 120,000 J over 150 J/K is 800 K.
All temperatures needs dH < 0 and dS > 0. Here dS is negative, so at high T the -T dS term wins.
120 is the size of dH in kJ, not a temperature. The crossover is dH divided by dS.
With dS < 0, heating makes dG more positive. Above 800 K the reaction is not spontaneous, so the range is below 800 K.

lockIt: dH and dS both negative: spontaneous below T = dH / dS. Both positive: spontaneous above it.

playWith.label: Gibbs module: set dH and dS both negative, slide T, and watch dG change sign

visual.reuse: new: chem.curve kind gibbs (tools/explain/visuals/chem-gc.js); the line is dG = dH - T dS from the stem values, and the build recomputes the crossover
visual.alt: A line plot of dG against temperature for dH = -120 kJ and dS = -150 J/K. The line starts at -120 kJ, rises, and crosses zero at 800 K, marked; the shaded part below zero is the spontaneous range, outlined under the axis as Below 800 K. Past 800 K a small shaded wedge sits above zero.
visual.caption: Follow the line up: it crosses zero at 800 K. Left of the crossing dG is negative, the spontaneous side.
